summary: Assessed 30 further distinct platform-focused leads: 28 projects promoted, one derivative converter excluded and one original-source archive identified as already-covered lineage.

project.title: DICE-nx
project.display_title: DICE-nx — restored Amiga C compiler toolchain
project.notes: Richard Downer's continuation of Matt Dillon's 1990s DICE, with compiler, assembler, linker, runtime libraries, debugger and build tools. Primary status documentation reports working native Amiga binaries on AmigaOS 3.2; the Linux/BSD bootstrap and subsequent self-hosting stages are distinct. No local build was run. NDK installation and some library variants require additional setup. CLAUDE.md and a co-authored commit establish present-day AI assistance; this says nothing about the original source's authorship.

identity.note: Checked repository root, primary README or source headers, source tree and latest commit. The record uses the coherent repository scope.

classification.note: Substantial restoration and continued development of the original DICE compiler suite, with an implemented 68k code generator, native assembly helpers, assembler, linker and runtime source. Qualifies as historical development-tool preservation and directly relevant native toolchain work.

source_cpu.note: README identifies the 68000-based Amiga DICE lineage; period src/dc1/gen.a contains native 68k compiler assembly, with 1992–1997 copyright headers.

target_cpu.note: README explicitly targets Amiga and embedded 68000 systems. src/dc1/asm1.c implements emitted assembly and machine.h defines data/address register allocation. No target CPU is inferred from the bootstrap host.

build.note: Welcome to DICE-nx.guide STATUS explicitly reports generated working Amiga binaries and restored native operation on real AmigaOS 3.2 hardware. Makefile shows stage1 bootstrap; later stages are self-hosted. Flags reflect upstream evidence, not a local reproduction.

runtime_profiles.note: README, user guide and CLAUDE.md were checked. The guide documents testing on AmigaOS 3.2 while CLAUDE.md describes a 1.3 compatibility floor; no verified minimum CPU/RAM profile is asserted.

ai.note: CLAUDE.md expressly addresses Claude Code; latest commit 8574873f0eaf2a0193f3cfdf880c56d6f379cfb5 also has a Claude co-author trailer. AI evidence concerns modern development.

relationships.note: README names DICE as the original code base and Richard Downer as DICE-nx maintainer, distinguishing it from Matt Dillon's original project. Compiler and companion tools form one suite.

next_actions: Reproduce the documented bootstrap and Amiga self-hosting stages if verified current build outputs are needed.

project.notes: Vesa Halttunen's 2021–2022 port translates the PET assembly game logic line by line into C++, with an AmigaOS platform layer, blitter tiles, ProTracker audio, gzip assets and native 68000 map/controller helpers. runtime_profiles.notes: README permits any classic Motorola 680x0 Amiga with at least 512 kB Chip RAM. With only 512 kB Chip RAM, in-game music is omitted in favour of effects. Its Add44k disk helper is incompatible with Kickstart 3.0 on low-memory configurations; total RAM and a universal OS floor are not asserted.

project.title: Phantom Fighter
project.display_title: Phantom Fighter — Amiga source archive and modern recreation
project.notes: Billy Newport's own recovered 1988 Amiga source and assets, PAL/NTSC variants, plus Python/Pygame and browser recreations. Original Lattice C/assembly uses KOS boot/disk support. README explicitly attributes the Python version to Claude; current JavaScript also has a Claude co-author commit. Modern paths directly implement entities, collision, scrolling and rendering, with no guest-CPU execution found. The modern DESIGN.md claims 68010 tuning, conflicting with the author's README account of 68000 development and 68010 incompatibility; no runtime minimum is asserted. Source/archive build reproducibility and modern playability are not locally verified.

project.title: hard-drivin-st
project.display_title: Hard Drivin' — archival source and incomplete Linux restoration
project.notes: Repository name, README and inherited C headers call the source Atari ST, but the reviewed implementation contains IBM/DOS interfaces and 16-bit x86 assembly: segmented far procedures, DOS mouse interrupt 33h, PC IRQ vectors and PIT port writes. These actual artifacts support DOS/x86 provenance; no m68k source or target is claimed. Current restoration replaces missing routines with warning/no-op stubs and uses host GCC; README's SDL2 port is an aim. The archive is described upstream as leaked source, so author-authorized release provenance is not established. Clean build/playability and modern host CPU remain unknown.

identity.note: Checked repository root, primary README or source headers, source tree and latest commit. The record uses the coherent repository scope.

classification.note: Concrete historical game-source restoration with substantial game logic and modified C build scaffolding. Actual x86/DOS code overrides the misleading ST repository label. Missing runtime stubs limit completeness but do not negate the existing archival/restoration work.

source_cpu.note: src/system.asm uses 16-bit x86 segmented far procedures and int 33h; src/setup.asm programs PC interrupt vectors and PIT ports 40h/43h. src/ibm.c retains commented DOS headers. README and inherited comments saying ST conflict with those artifacts; only verified x86 is recorded.

target_cpu.note: Makefile selects generic host GCC and has no architecture target flag. Linux is the stated restoration target, but exact host CPU is unknown; no m68k output path was established.

Original C#/MonoGame re-creation of the CPC Airwolf gameplay with real level, enemy, helicopter, collision and UI code. Creator explicitly says it is not emulation, recreates only gameplay and may omit original features. This is a modern remake, not a native CPC port or a claimed disassembly.

Substantive CPC C/assembly development framework, low-level hardware library, asset tools and reproducible-project build infrastructure. Inspected keyboard implementation directly programs the PPI/PSG; examples and content tools form the same coherent repository.

Author-maintained C Z80 cross-assembler includes CPC cartridge/snapshot/disk/tape generation, integrated compression, patching support and debug symbols. Inspected actual assembler source, integrated API example and build files. Z80 is the output instruction set, not a claim that the host executable runs on Z80.

Original author preserved and annotated the commercial 1985 CPC DAMS source, with a tokenized-source encoder/decoder and documented self-hosting rebuild procedure. Actual dams.dams assembly and C++ conversion tool establish substantive source restoration, not a binary-only distribution.

Concrete fast CPC tape loader with adaptive pulse measurement, synchronization and native loading code, paired with a Python CDT generator. Source credits Mert Boru's TurboLoader as the basis; this repository adds an implemented paired workflow rather than a passive binary mirror.

Author-maintained native diagnostic suite tests RAM, ROM, keyboard and CRTC behavior, with substantial hardware routines and distinct ROM, RAM, cartridge, disk and tape build variants. Companion ROM dump code supports retro system investigation.

Creator-published multi-platform native adventure game source, with substantial CPC/C64 C game code and Amiga assembly implementation plus asset/build tools. Track the common game once at repository scope; referenced Spectrum/ST ports are not claimed as present in this repository.

decisions.title: DICE-nx — restored Amiga C compiler toolchain
decisions.reason: Substantial restoration and continued development of the original DICE compiler suite, with an implemented 68k code generator, native assembly helpers, assembler, linker and runtime source. Qualifies as historical development-tool preservation and directly relevant native toolchain work.

decisions.title: Parcade — native Amiga demo source
decisions.reason: Creator-published, substantial native 68000 Amiga intro implementation with multiple effects, hardware takeover/restore, music integration and assembly instructions. Track the complete intro rather than separate effect files.

decisions.title: Attack of the PETSCII Robots — native Amiga translation
decisions.reason: Substantial native fan conversion with first-person development notes, translated C++ game logic and Amiga-specific assembly/rendering. Source translation, not embedded guest-CPU emulation.

decisions.title: Phantom Fighter — Amiga source archive and modern recreation
decisions.reason: Creator-published recovery of substantial original 1988 Amiga game code plus concrete source-based native Python/JavaScript recreations. The modern paths implement game logic directly and do not use game-specific CPU pseudo-emulation.

decisions.title: Devil's Temple — native Amiga game source
decisions.reason: Substantial creator-attributed native Amiga homebrew/spin-off implementation, corroborated by the creator's released-game page. Actual game source extends far beyond a copied loader/template.

decisions.title: Alpha Waves — original Atari ST source archive
decisions.reason: Substantive original Atari ST game source and assets, with author/date headers and concrete 68k game/polygon implementation. Historical preservation qualifies independently of unknown buildability; not labelled a binary-derived disassembly.

decisions.title: Hard Drivin' — archival source and incomplete Linux restoration
decisions.reason: Concrete historical game-source restoration with substantial game logic and modified C build scaffolding. Actual x86/DOS code overrides the misleading ST repository label. Missing runtime stubs limit completeness but do not negate the existing archival/restoration work.

decisions.title: Alice Personal Pascal — historical IDE source and portability work
decisions.reason: Substantial period programming environment with preserved Atari ST/Unix source, interpreter, editor, debugger and actual portability scaffolding. Qualifies as historical development-tool preservation, not a tutorial or unrelated modern application.

decisions.title: StingRay GamePatches — Amiga compatibility fixes and trainers
decisions.reason: Concrete binary-derived patch implementations, identified game offsets and documented compatibility defects. A small README is unnecessary: source comments and substantive assembly establish the work. Track the coherent patch collection at repository scope.

decisions.title: FujiBoink — original ST source archive
decisions.reason: Preserves the original 1986 FujiBoink C/68000 demo source and period documentation. The already tracked mnemo70/fujiboink conversion repository retains the same six historical ST source components under st_source, with matching creator/date headers and implementation. Retain this useful original-source reference linked to that lineage, without adding a second overlapping source-only project. All six historical C/assembly components match after whitespace normalization; five match with CRLF normalization alone.

decisions.title: Ghost Town — C16 disassembly and native Commodore ports
decisions.reason: Substantial annotated Ghost Town recovery includes original-platform logic, bug fixes, languages, graphics, SID music and native C64/C128 conversion. The two ports and supporting tools are one coherent repository-wide project.

decisions.title: C64 crack-intro disassemblies — Tomaszndt
decisions.reason: Five source listings contain concrete C64 intro disassembly with origin links, labels and analysis of raster interrupts, scrolling, system calls and music. Lack of a README/build script does not negate the existing research; catalogue at whole-repository scope.

decisions.title: Music-player disassemblies — C64 and Atari 8-bit
decisions.reason: Concrete labelled disassembly and sequencer/pattern analysis of C64 International Karate SID and multiple Atari POKEY players, accompanied by Frida projects and source music files. This is subsystem research rather than full-game reconstruction and is kept as one coherent archive.

decisions.title: c64-ruby — C64 assets, code generation and build tools
decisions.reason: Implemented Ruby library provides VIC-II image conversion, 6502 assembly/byte generation, PRG merging, VICE snapshot injection and ca65/ld65/Exomizer build automation. It is directly relevant development tooling beyond its short library overview.

decisions.title: Bitmapper — C64 multicolor bitmap converter
decisions.reason: Concrete Java/Swing cross-development tool converts images to C64 multicolor data and exports Koala files, with palette selection, per-cell color constraints, dithering and a GUI. The nested NetBeans project is the repository's single tool.

decisions.title: oscar64nvim — C64 build and debug integration
decisions.reason: Working implementation exists for project-aware Oscar64 compile commands, asynchronous process handling, Quickfix compiler diagnostics, assembly viewing and VICE/RetroDebugger launch. This is a distinct Neovim integration, not an independent compiler/emulator.

decisions.title: Mutant Monty — native Amiga Scorpion conversion
decisions.reason: Creator-published Scorpion source contains substantial Mutant Monty game logic, actors, 41 level maps, graphics and sound, with released Amiga ADF/WHDLoad builds linked from the creator page. It qualifies as a native fan conversion; original C64/CPC binary analysis is not claimed.

decisions.title: Mars Patrol — creator-restored C64 Moon Patrol conversion
decisions.reason: Creator documents recovery of his unfinished 1985 C64 Moon Patrol conversion by disassembling and reassembling the old binary in 2024, then implementing substantial missing gameplay. Published PRG/D64 outputs and explicit PAL VICE play testing support a concrete restoration even though recovered source files are not published.

decisions.title: Lawn Job — author-restored C64 BASIC source
decisions.reason: Michael Buhidar republishes and verifies his own 1983/84 C64 BASIC game from the October 1984 Ahoy! type-in. Complete game listing and tokenized PRG are present, with original-author provenance, line-check verification and explicit VICE operation.

decisions.title: c64_disassembly_reader — derivative hex-listing converter
decisions.reason: README identifies this as a converter of mist64/c64disasm's existing hex-assembly text into BASIC/KERNAL binary images. c64_read_dis.erl parses listed addresses/bytes, fills address gaps and writes bytes; it adds no independent disassembly, recovery analysis or substantive compiler. Excluded under the workflow's rule for merely converting somebody else's analysis; original listing attribution is preserved.

decisions.title: Knight Lore CPC reconstruction
decisions.reason: RAM-derived CPC Knight Lore reconstruction contains symbolic Z80 assembly, data extraction and detailed engine analysis, with original and experimental rendering branches. Primary main-branch documentation reports successful RASM assembly and standalone snapshot boot to the real menu. This does not establish full playability or complete byte matching; the browser component is described only as a room visualizer.
